title: Chapter XXIV

teacherSummary.text: Walton resumes writing. The ice traps the ship; the crew demands to turn south, and Walton yields. Victor dies. The creature appears over his body, mourns, condemns himself, and vows to destroy himself on a funeral pyre before vanishing into darkness.

Setting: The Arctic ice traps the ship; the crew demands return. Watch for light and fire: Light stands for knowledge and fire for its double edge: warmth and burning. Victor seeks the "light" of discovery; the creature discovers fire and is burned by it. In this chapter: “to execute this dear revenge, will I again behold the sun, and tread the green herbage of earth, which otherwise should vanish” (Chapter XXIV, paragraph 5).

segments.script: First, meaning. I read “Seek happiness in tranquillity, and avoid ambition” slowly and put it in my own words: Dying, Victor tells Walton to seek happiness in tranquillity and avoid ambition. Next, craft. I notice the calm, moral tone of a dying man, a sharp change from his fevered story. The strongest word is “ambition”: it names the fault that drove him to create life and destroy his family. Then, effect. What final advice does Victor give Walton, and does he mean it? My answer: Victor warns against ambition, yet in the next breath admits another man may succeed where he failed; his mixed message leaves Walton, who turns his ship home, to choose wisely where Victor could not.
